Syncly.subtitle: Professional Networking Platform
Syncly.description: Syncly is a full-stack professional networking platform Vigneshwaran built from scratch, designed to help individuals, researchers, and professionals across diverse sectors (Tech, Biology, Commerce, IT, and more) connect, collaborate, and share projects. Unlike traditional networking apps, Syncly emphasises real collaboration through swipe-based matchmaking (right swipe = Vibe to connect, left swipe = Ghost to skip), real-time chat via Socket.IO with typing indicators and active user tracking, a custom portfolio builder (users generate a professional responsive portfolio by filling out forms — no coding required), AWS SES integration for onboarding and notification emails with cron-based daily collaboration summaries, and scalable modular REST APIs. Deployed on AWS EC2.
Syncly.role: Solo full-stack development, backend APIs, AWS deployment
highlights: Real-time chat with typing indicators and active user tracking
AWS SES email automation with daily cron summaries

GlycanBench.subtitle: Glycomics AI Platform
GlycanBench.description: GlycanBench is an interactive glycomics research platform hosted at SASTRA University. It lets researchers analyze, visualize, and manipulate glycan structures. Vigneshwaran integrated multiple deep learning models — BiLSTM, XGBoost, GAT, GIN, MPNN — for immunogenicity prediction, achieving up to 98.2% accuracy. The platform also supports motif extraction and mutation analysis. Backend is FastAPI/Flask (Python), frontend is React.js with Tailwind CSS.
GlycanBench.role: ML model development and evaluation, full-stack development

EGFR Inhibitors for Ovarian Cancer.subtitle: Drug Discovery via Explainable AI
EGFR Inhibitors for Ovarian Cancer.description: Vigneshwaran built an explainable ML framework to discover potent EGFR inhibitors targeting ovarian cancer. Using ChEMBL bioactivity data, he built a cheminformatics pipeline with RDKit and Mordred for 1800+ molecular descriptors. After Lasso feature selection, Gradient Boosting achieved 92% accuracy and Random Forest 94.28%. SHAP explanations identified key molecular features (PEOE_VSA9, SM_VSA10, pic50) and produced force/waterfall plots for interpretability.

Prediction of lignocellulosic components.subtitle: ML for Green Energy · Biomass Pretreatment
Prediction of lignocellulosic components.description: This study explores efficient bioethanol production from waste biomass using an integrated approach of nanotechnology, green pretreatment methods, and machine learning. Twenty different lignocellulosic biomass samples (mainly fruit peels and agro-wastes) were pretreated using physical, chemical, and novel physicochemical methods — including nanocatalyst-assisted ionic liquid combined with ultrasound — to extract fermentable sugars. Iron nanoparticles synthesised from Musa acuminata peels improved biomass breakdown. Machine learning models — Decision Tree, Random Forest, and LGBM — were trained on experimental data to predict biomass composition and ethanol yield. Random Forest and Decision Tree showed high accuracy in predicting lignocellulosic content and sugar yield. A BFuel web platform was developed to store and display experimental data.
key_contributions: Eco-friendly biomass pretreatment using nanotechnology and ionic liquids
Multiple ML algorithms for predictive modeling of biomass composition and ethanol yield
BFuel web-based database for managing biomass and bioethanol data

QSPR for Posaconazole SEDDS.subtitle: Pharmaceutical Formulation Modeling
QSPR for Posaconazole SEDDS.description: QSPR models to predict Posaconazole solubility in Self-Emulsifying Drug Delivery Systems (SEDDS). Formulation components encoded with quantum chemical descriptors. VIF analysis eliminated multicollinearity. Random Forest achieved R² up to 0.926, outperforming MLR, KNN, and SVM.

Suitability Studies Of Fruits Of West In.subtitle: Biofuel Feedstock Evaluation
Suitability Studies Of Fruits Of West In.description: Investigated the potential of Guazuma ulmifolia (West Indian Elm) fruits as a feedstock for biofuel production. Fruits were ground into powder and extracted using solvent extraction with petroleum ether. Confirmatory tests for lipids (emulsion and acrolein assays) were performed on the solvent-vaporised residue. The processed biomass was subjected to H₂SO₄ acid hydrolysis followed by heat treatment and tested for fermentable sugars. The sample contained no lipids but did contain carbohydrates, supporting bioethanol potential over biodiesel. Future work focuses on comparative analysis of solvent extraction versus nano-catalysts and enzymatic pretreatment for improved sugar yield.
Suitability Studies Of Fruits Of West In.findings: No lipids detected; carbohydrates confirmed — supports bioethanol over biodiesel pathway
